titulo: Food: partitives, quantities and the restaurant: Food and the partitives

aula.titulo: Food: partitives, quantities and the restaurant
aula.objetivo: Talk about what you eat and drink with the partitive articles («du», «de la», «de l'», «des»), express quantities, and order in a café or restaurant with «je voudrais» and «prendre».

blocos.titulo: Du, de la, de l', des: a part of something
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: to talk about an unspecified amount of something you eat or drink, use the partitive article: «du» (masculine), «de la» (feminine), «de l'» (vowel), «des» (plural). «Je mange du pain.» «Je bois de la limonade.» «Je bois de l'eau.» «Je mange des légumes.» STEP 2: the partitive is like «some» or «a bit of», which English often leaves out: «I eat bread». STEP 3: with «aimer», «adorer» and «détester», use the definite article: «J'aime le pain.» (I like it in general) vs. «Je mange du pain.» (I'm eating some bread). STEP 4: in the negative, the partitive becomes «de» (or «d'»): «Je ne mange pas de viande.» «Il n'y a pas d'eau.» STEP 5: after an expression of quantity, you also use «de» without an article: «beaucoup de pain», «un peu d'eau», «trop de sel». STEP 6: the verb «manger» changes its spelling with «nous»: «nous mangeons». The verb «boire» is irregular: «je bois, tu bois, il boit, nous buvons, vous buvez, ils boivent».
blocos.comparacao: in English we say «I eat bread» and «I drink water», with no article. In French the article is required: «je mange du pain», «je bois de l'eau». This is the biggest difference between the two languages at the table.

tabela.example: Je ne mange pas de viande.

erros.errado: Je ne mange pas du pain.
erros.certo: Je ne mange pas de pain.
erros.motivo: In the negative, the partitive becomes «de».

blocos.enunciado: Say what you eat and drink for breakfast and lunch, and what you don't eat: «Je mange du… Je bois de l'… Je ne mange pas de…»
Give directions from one place to another in your city, with prepositions and directions.
